chunks: And Ismaʿil ibn Muslim narrated from al-Sadiq Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAli عليه السلام:

That the testimony of children, if they testified while they were young, is valid when they grow older so long as they have not forgotten it. Likewise, the testimony of the Jews and the Christians, if they accept Islam, is valid. And the slave, if he is called to bear testimony and then is emancipated, his testimony is valid if the judge did not reject it before he was emancipated.
And he عليه السلام said: “If the slave was emancipated for the sake of the testimony, his testimony is not valid.”

key_terms.أَسْلَمُوا: they embraced Islam, affecting legal acceptance of testimony
key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: was emancipated or freed from slavery
key_terms.الصِّبْيَانِ: young children whose testimony is discussed in relation to later maturity
key_terms.النَّصَارَى: Christians whose testimony is mentioned upon embracing Islam
key_terms.الْحَاكِمُ: the judge who may accept or reject testimony
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: a slave whose testimony is considered after emancipation
key_terms.الْيَهُودُ: Jews whose testimony is mentioned upon embracing Islam
key_terms.شَهَادَةَ: legal testimony given before an authority

ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of children, converts, and freed slaves accepted in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith presents legal rulings concerning the acceptance of testimony in court. It states that prior impediments to testimony may be removed later in some cases, such as a child reaching maturity, a non-Muslim embracing Islam, or a slave being emancipated, provided the testimony remains intact and is not manipulated for judicial purposes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3295 - And it was narrated by Isma'il ibn Muslim, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), from his father Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), from his forefathers, from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), who said:

"The testimony of children, if they testified while they were young, is valid when they grow older as long as they have not forgotten it. Likewise, the testimony of Jews and Christians, if they embrace Islam, is valid. Also, the testimony of a slave, if he was made to testify and then was freed, is valid as long as the judge did not reject it before his emancipation."

And Imam (as) said:
"If the slave was freed specifically for the purpose of testimony, his testimony is not valid."
